projects.name: Template Studio
projects.description: Turn everyday announcements into consistent, ready to export designs.
projects.scope: All seven English template routes were exercised in the original browser editor. Each Download JPG action produced a readable JPEG with nonzero dimensions, with no broken browser images or download failures. The recording shows the original selection, editing and preview workflow.
projects.role: Solo creator · Product, design and engineering
projects.ownership: I designed and built this project independently, including its interface and implementation.
projects.problem: Routine institutional announcements share a visual system but carry different names, dates and contact details. Recreating each layout manually makes consistency harder to maintain.
projects.contribution: I designed and built the template collection, editing forms, live previews and image export, including the layout rules for each announcement type.
projects.implementation: Typed template data feeds React layouts. The editor measures the available space to scale its preview, while export uses the original canvas dimensions and embedded fonts.
projects.result: A user can choose a template, enter the announcement details and export a JPG. Seven template routes cover appointment, departure, HR information, condolences and celebrations.

projects.problem: Working with a coding agent involves more than sending a prompt. Sessions, streamed output, tool approvals and model settings need to stay understandable as work progresses.
projects.contribution: I designed and built the macOS application: the session browser, live conversation interface, controls and integration with the dsh server.
projects.implementation: SwiftUI presents sessions while JSON RPC and a WebSocket event stream connect the interface to the existing dsh harness. History recovery reads the local session log when the server cannot serve a damaged transcript.
projects.result: The application brings session navigation, streaming output, approvals and configuration into one native workspace. The original repository includes the demonstration shown here.

projects.name: Sift

projects.scope: Existing English browser version; 18 synthetic sessions indexed, pagination search and session reading verified in browser; 31 tests passed and terminal POST returned 403. Native clients not exercised.
projects.role: Solo creator · Product, design and engineering
projects.ownership: I designed and built this project independently, including its interface and implementation.
projects.problem: Useful decisions and solutions accumulate across Claude Code and Codex transcripts. Remembering a previous solution does not necessarily mean remembering which session contains it.
projects.contribution: I designed and built Sift, from transcript ingestion and local indexing to the search interface and the flow for returning to a session.
projects.implementation: Provider specific readers normalize local transcripts into a SQLite index. FTS5 provides full text search with ranked results. The interface can open the original session in the appropriate agent.
projects.result: Search, filters and readable session details provide a route back to earlier work. The demonstration uses example transcripts with the real indexing and reading flow.
